   "Berenberg's baseline assumes the Iran war's oil shock is temporary. Brent falls to $75 per barrel by late 2027 and averages $65 by late 2028. The bank expects Republicans, after heavy midterm losses, to push Trump to resolve the conflict soon.",
   "Berenberg assumes Trump will not noticeably raise the average US tariff rate again, because high prices are unpopular. A renewed tariff escalation would do more damage to the US and global economy than the forecasts embody.",
   "Global GDP growth (market exchange rates) is forecast at 2.6% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 and 2.4% in 2028. The bank's weights are US 26.4%, China 16.9% and Eurozone 14.8%.",
   "US: AI investment and fiscal stimulus keep growth above 2% for now (2.3% in 2026, 2.0% in 2027). Without immigration, productivity gains must carry growth, and Berenberg doubts AI will deliver enough of them fast enough. Growth is forecast to slow to the 1.5% trend rate by 2028.",
   "US consumption increasingly depends on high-income households, who hold more wealth in equities and face less inflation pressure. The economy is therefore sensitive to an equity market correction tied to AI returns.",
   "US policy: Berenberg expects the Fed under Kevin Warsh to raise the funds rate twice more by end of Q1 2027, to 4.25%-4.50%, because of elevated energy prices and sticky core inflation. It sees US CPI at 3.5% in 2026 and 2.6% in 2027.",
   "US long-term drag: the immigration crackdown, tariffs, institutional erosion and the Iran war have cut trend growth from 2.0% to 1.5%. Berenberg flags a growing risk of a bond-market buyers' strike that forces a major fiscal adjustment. It forecasts the federal deficit at 6.3% of GDP in 2026 and 6.5% in 2027.",
   "China: growth is forecast at 4.6% in 2026 and 2027 and 4.2% in 2028. Weak consumer confidence, reluctant business investment, property sector troubles and anti-dumping measures in key export markets weigh on it. The modest monetary and fiscal stimulus is judged temporary because it does not address structural problems.",
   "Japan: Berenberg expects three more 25bp BoJ hikes, taking the policy rate to 2.00%, with quantitative tightening continuing. GDP growth is forecast at 0.9% in 2026 and 2027. Fiscal stimulus from PM Takaichi could surprise to the upside.",
   "Japan risk: inflation expectations are still fragile after decades of deflation, so higher energy prices could hit demand harder than elsewhere. If cost-push inflation feeds into larger pay rises, the BoJ would fall behind the curve.",
   "UK: the BoE raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4.00% in Q4. Berenberg sees it on hold at 4.00% by mid-2027, then cutting to 3.75% by end-2027 and 3.50% by end-2028, and notes lower inflation than the BoE expects could mean no further hike. GDP growth is 1.6% in 2026, 1.5% in 2027 and 1.8% in 2028.",
   "UK risks: a permanent loss of Persian Gulf energy exports would keep energy prices high and raise inflation and GDP damage. The bond market would punish any dilution of fiscal consolidation.",
   "Eurozone (ex Ireland): GDP growth is forecast at 1.2% in 2026, 1.1% in 2027 and a cyclical peak of 1.7% in 2028. Defence and infrastructure spending support domestic demand. Including Ireland, 2026 growth is about 1.0%.",
   "ECB: after hikes in June and September, Berenberg expects a December hike taking the deposit rate to 2.75%, which it considers a mistake given the Iran war's drag on demand. It expects no further moves in 2027 and 2028 unless wage inflation accelerates.",
   "Eurozone inflation risk: if energy prices spike further, inflation could stay near 4% for longer, reducing real household spending power and triggering more ECB hikes.",
   "Germany: the loosened debt brake means deficits above 3% of GDP, adding about 0.3ppt to demand in 2026. GDP growth is forecast at 1.0% in 2026, 0.9% in 2027 and 1.6% in 2028. A planned reform package (pensions, taxes, labour law, bureaucracy) could lift growth more than the fiscal stimulus if fully implemented.",
   "France: a creeping fiscal crisis. The 2026 deficit is likely 5.4% of GDP and the minority government is struggling to stop it rising to 6% in 2027. Berenberg sees a full-blown crisis as a clear risk but not yet likely, and says the ECB would only help if Paris meets fiscal conditions. Spring 2027 elections could tilt policy toward expensive, protectionist agendas.",
   "Italy: growth is forecast at 0.8% in 2026 and 0.6% in 2027, with NextGenerationEU support fading in 2027. Italy is more exposed to the Iran war shock than other large Eurozone members because of its gas import dependence. Berenberg's 2027 inflation forecast (3.2%) is well above consensus (2.6%).",
   "Spain: growth stays well above the Eurozone average (2.6% in 2026, 2.3% in 2027). Elections on 29 November could bring a more pro-reform centre-right government in 2027.",
   "Portugal: growth is forecast at 2.3% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, with the Iran war a modest near-term downside risk. Public finances are roughly balanced.",
